faq_heading: Quay condos and townhomes: your questions answered

blocks.text: Draft for Jared's approval. Built only from the monthly MLS® figures (SnapStats) for condos and townhomes in Quay. No local notes, sold prices, building list or live listing feed yet; see the open items.

Quay, New Westminster: 59 condos and townhomes listed at the end of September 2026 and 16 sold in the month, a sales ratio of 27%, which the reports’ scale reads as a sellers’ market. By listings that is number 4 of 14 New Westminster communities for condos and townhomes.

blocks.text: Listings of condos and townhomes in Quay fell from 68 in June to 59 in September (−13.2%), and 51 sold across the 4 months. In September the community held 13.3% of New Westminster’s 444 condos and townhomes listed.

blocks.text: Quay home prices: what sold, November 2025 to October 2026

127 condos sold in Quay with a median price of $630,000 (the middle half sold between $545,000 and $731,000), taking a median of 28 days to sell at 97.3% of the last list price; 9% sold above list. They had a median $632 per square foot, a median year built of 2006 and a median strata fee of $591 a month.

Streets, schools and getting around Quay

items.t: Where the condo stock concentrates: this sub-area is almost entirely condos. The stock lines Quayside Drive from Westminster Pier Park east along the Waterfront Esplanade: the 2019 Bosa towers at the west end (RiverSky 1 and 2), the 1989–1990s Bosa-era towers mid-drive (Anchor Pointe, Riviera, Tiffany Shores, The Promenade), the Laguna Court cluster (Laguna Landing, The Excelsior), and the Aragon buildings at the Renaissance Square / Rialto Court pocket (The Q, Murano Lofts), plus two 1980s wood-frame low-rises (Quay West, Quayside Terrace).

Transit anchors: New Westminster Station and Columbia Station (Expo Line) at the top of the waterfront; TransLink route 103 is the Quayside / New Westminster Station route and route 102 serves Victoria Hill / New Westminster Station. Quayside Drive is the waterfront road; Columbia Street and 8th Street link the Quay to Downtown and the station, and Stewardson Way links west toward Marine Way and Burnaby.

Waterfront anchors: Westminster Pier Park at 600 Quayside Drive, Quayside Park (with a water play area) and the Waterfront Esplanade boardwalk run the length of the waterfront; a library kiosk and holds locker are at the Anvil Centre, 777 Columbia Street, at the top of the waterfront.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Quay

items.t: Floodplain — the Quay's defining rule: the City's floodplain study places the Quay in Floodplain Zone 3, the Fraser River waterfront zone, where many newer buildings have floor space above the Flood Construction Level but egress and the waterfront path sit below it. The City publishes flood management information for its low-lying zones including the Quay; confirm the specific building's flood construction level compliance and the strata's insurance and deductible position lot by lot before subject removal.

blocks.text: Good to know about Quay

items.t: The living space is above the flood level; the way out is not. The City's floodplain study notes that in Zone 3 many newer buildings have floor space above the Flood Construction Level, but egress and the waterfront path sit below it — a distinction that shapes strata insurance and emergency planning, and one that listing copy never mentions.

One developer built most of the waterfront, in two waves. Bosa built the first wave (Anchor Pointe 1989, Riviera 1990 per the building-data sources) and the current wave (RiverSky 1 and 2, both 2019; Pier West beside Pier Park) — cross-building comparisons of construction and warranty inside the Quay are unusually direct because so much stock shares one builder.

The Quay has two names and both are official in different places. The board sub-area name is "Quay" (SnapStats GVR); the City's heritage context name for the same neighbourhood is "Quayside," and the street, park and bus route all use Quayside. Searches under only one name miss records filed under the other.

Tiffany Shores is four addresses, one strata. 1210, 1220, 1230 and 1240 Quayside Drive sit under a single strata corporation, NWS2924, managed by Quay Pacific — document orders and depreciation reports run to the corporation, not to the individual street address.

The city's newest recreation asset is up the hill, not on the waterfront. The təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre at 65 East Sixth Avenue fully opened in May 2024 — at 10,644 sq. m. the City's largest capital project to date, with an eight-lane 50-metre pool, leisure pool, fitness centre and gymnasia.

blocks.text: Townhome complexes in Quay
Streets, schools and getting around Quay

items.t: Where the stock sits: high-rise and mid-rise apartment buildings along Quayside Drive and its court streets (Renaissance Square, Rialto Court, Reliance Court, K de K Court, Laguna Court).

Transit and roads: New Westminster Station and Columbia Station (Expo Line) serve the Quay at the top of the waterfront; TransLink route 103 is the Quayside / New Westminster Station route and route 102 serves Victoria Hill / New Westminster Station. Quayside Drive is the waterfront road; Columbia Street and 8th Street link the Quay to Downtown, and Stewardson Way links west toward Marine Way and Burnaby.

Schools: SD40 catchments are address-based. For the sample address 800 Carnarvon Street (the New Westminster Station address), the SD40 School Locator returns École Qayqayt Elementary (K–5), Fraser River Middle (6–8) and New Westminster Secondary (9–12); Quayside Drive addresses can differ, and no home is promised a specific school.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect townhome buyers in Quay

items.t: Floodplain Zone 3 is the defining diligence item for Quayside stock — townhouse-form units included: the City's floodplain study places the Quay in Floodplain Zone 3, the Fraser River waterfront zone, where many newer buildings have floor space above the Flood Construction Level but egress and the waterfront path sit below it. For a ground-oriented townhouse unit at a tower's base, confirm the unit's own floor level against the building's Flood Construction Level compliance, plus the strata insurance and deductible position, before subject removal.

Form B diligence (every strata complex in, including RiverSky 2's townhouse units): Strata Property Act s. 59 — the Form B states the lot's monthly strata fees, amounts owing, approved special levies still payable, the CRF balance and an insurance summary, with the rules, current budget, any Rental Disclosure Statement and the most recent depreciation report attached; provided within 7 days, maximum $35 plus up to 25 cents per page. A townhouse unit inside a tower strata is a strata lot like any other — there is no separate townhouse Form B.

blocks.text: Good to know about Quay

items.t: The Quay has a library presence without a branch: a library kiosk and holds locker sit at the Anvil Centre, 777 Columbia Street, at the top of the waterfront, while the Main Branch is at 716 6th Avenue in Uptown.

The city's hospital is one SkyTrain ride east: Royal Columbian Hospital, 330 East Columbia Street in Sapperton (Fraser Health), east of the Quay by SkyTrain — relevant to the downsizer buyers this waterfront draws.

The təməsew̓txʷ Aquatic and Community Centre, 65 East Sixth Avenue, fully opened in May 2024 — at 10,644 sq. m. the City's largest capital project to date, with an eight-lane 50-metre pool — and it sits up the hill from the Quay, not on the waterfront, despite how listings phrase it.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes are for sale in Quay?
faq.a: At the end of September 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 59 condos and townhomes listed in Quay. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Quay a buyers’ or sellers’ market for condos and townhomes?
faq.a: In September 2026, condos and townhomes in Quay had a sales ratio of 27%, which the reports’ scale reads as a sellers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many condos and townhomes sold in Quay from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 51 condos and townhomes sold in Quay over those 4 months, out of 261 in all of New Westminster.

faq.q: Do these numbers separate condos from townhomes?
faq.a: No. The monthly reports publish condos and townhomes as one line, so every count here includes both. Jared can pull the split for a specific building or street.

faq.q: What did condos in Quay sell for?
faq.a: 127 condos sold in Quay between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $630,000.

faq.q: How long do condos take to sell in Quay?
faq.a: The median was 28 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 97.3% of the last list price (9% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.

faq.q: Is the Quay in the floodplain?
faq.a: Yes — the City's floodplain study puts the Quay in Floodplain Zone 3, where many newer buildings have floor space above the Flood Construction Level but egress and the waterfront path sit below it. The practical questions are building-specific: flood construction level compliance, strata insurance cover and deductibles, and any flood-related claims history in the strata documents.

faq.q: Which buildings are the newest, and does warranty remain?
faq.a: RiverSky 1 (908 Quayside Drive) and RiverSky 2 (988 Quayside Drive) were both built in 2019 by Bosa Properties — 33-storey concrete towers of 233 and 234 units.

faq.q: Is there any low-rise or wood-frame stock, or is it all towers?
faq.a: Mostly towers, but not all: Quay West (31 Reliance Court) is a 4-storey, 60-unit wood-frame low-rise built in 1986, Quayside Terrace (5 K de K Court) is a 4-storey building, and Murano Lofts (7 Rialto Court) is a 7-storey concrete mid-rise of 237 units built in 2005. Wood-frame versus concrete changes the insurance, depreciation-report and levy conversation — check which form the specific building is.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Quay condo long-term?
faq.a: Yes — strata rental-restriction bylaws have been unenforceable since November 24, 2022 anywhere in BC, whatever older directory or bylaw text says. Short-term rentals are different: a strata bylaw can still restrict them, and the registered bylaws on the Form B govern that question.

faq.q: The Riviera's address and year don't match between sources — which is right?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED. Treat them as an unresolved conflict and verify the strata plan number on the specific unit's title before relying on either set of figures.

faq.q: Is there a townhouse complex on the Quay?
faq.a: No standalone one — the verified count is 0 strata and 0 fee-simple. The waterfront's stock is apartment stratas; the closest townhouse-form product is the TH-series homes at the base of RiverSky 2, which are strata lots inside that tower's plan (EPS5412).

faq.q: What does Floodplain Zone 3 mean for my purchase?
faq.a: The Quay is the City's Fraser River waterfront flood zone: many newer buildings have floor space above the Flood Construction Level, but egress and the waterfront path sit below it. Confirm the specific building's compliance and insurance position lot by lot, especially for ground-level units.

faq.q: Can I rent out a Quay strata home long-term?
faq.a: Yes under provincial law: strata rental-restriction bylaws have been void since Nov 24, 2022. Short-term rentals can still be restricted by bylaw — read the registered bylaws in the Form B package.
